newsitem.title: USA: Conn. May unemployment rate steady at 5.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: Conn. May unemployment rate steady at 5.2 percent.

text.p: Connecticut's May jobless rate held steady at 5.2 percent from April as gains in all but two sectors pushed the rate four-tenths of a percentage point below the year-ago level, according to the state Department of Labor.

"Despite the unchanged jobless rate over the month, the year-to-year labor force increase of 23,700 suggests that an improved economy is encouraging more people to seek employment," said the state labor statistics supervisor, Salvatore DiPillo, in prepared remarks released on Tuesday.

The service industry added 2,900 positions, exceeding wholesale and retail trade, which grew by 1,500, construction and mining, up 1,000, transportation, coummunications and utilities, rising 700, and finance, insurance and real estate, up 500. The government sector lost 1,500 jobs, while manufacturing positions fell by 500.
The following list details a number of labor markets within in the state.
--Bridgeport, 5.8 pct, up from 5.7 pct in April but down from 6.5 percent a year-ago.
--Danbury, 3.2 percent, up from 3.1 percent in April, but down from 3.7 percent year-ago.
--Danielson, 6.2 percent, up from 5.9 percent in April, down from 6.4 percent a year-ago.
--Hartford, 5.3 percent, up from 5.0 percent in April, down from 5.9 percent a year-ago.
--Lower River, 3.8 percent, up from 3.3 percent in April, down from 4.1 percent a year-ago.
--New Haven, 5.3 percent, down from 5.4 percent in Ap;ril, 5.6 percent a year-ago.
--New London, 5.5 percent, up from 4.9 percent in April, and 5.2 percent a year-ago.
--Stamford, 3.1 percent, up from 2.9 percent in April, down from 3.6 percent a year-ago.
--Torrington, 3.8 percent, down from 4.1 percent in April, 4.6 percent a year-ago.
--Waterbury, 5.7 percent, down from 5.8 percent in April, 6.1 percent a year-ago.
